title: Path traversal via unnormalised archive entry names in extractAll()
summary: extractAll() joins each archive entry's stored name onto the destination directory without normalising it or verifying the result stays inside that directory. An archive containing an entry named ../../tmp/pwned causes a write outside the destination. The entry name is attacker-controlled whenever a consumer extracts an archive it did not author, which is the library's documented purpose.

versions_tested.note: Current release at time of testing.

trace.code: export async function extractAll(archivePath, destDir, opts = {}) {
trace.note: Documented public API. The archive is third-party data by design; the README's first example extracts a downloaded release tarball.
Entry name read verbatim from the archive header. No normalisation, no rejection of absolute paths or traversal segments.
path.join collapses traversal segments but does not confine the result to destDir. path.resolve followed by a prefix check would; neither is present.
Write occurs at the traversed path, with the mode stored in the archive.

reachability.entrypoint: extractAll(archivePath, destDir) — the library's primary documented export
reachability.missing_guard: No path.resolve + startsWith(destDir) confinement check between reader.js:118 and writer.js:77.
reachability.note: No option gates the behaviour. opts.strict exists but only controls checksum verification; it does not affect entry-name handling.

conditions.description: The consumer must extract an archive from an untrusted source. This is the library's documented use case rather than a limiting condition, but it is stated because a consumer that only extracts archives it produced itself is unaffected.

The process must have write permission to the traversed destination. Writing to a privileged path requires a privileged process; under an unprivileged user the impact is confined to paths that user can already write.

severity.justification: Arbitrary file write within the extracting process's permissions, demonstrated by writing outside destDir. Scored UI:R because a consumer action (extracting) is required, and I:H because the PoC overwrote an arbitrary file. NOT scored Critical: no privilege escalation or code execution was demonstrated, only the write. Severity is capped at what the PoC actually showed, not at what a write could lead to.

confidence.justification: For this to be wrong, path.join would have to confine results to destDir, which it does not, or a caller-side check would have to reject the entry name before writer.js:63. The whole call path was read at the pinned SHA and no such check exists. The PoC ran three times from a clean container and the negative control failed as expected on 2.4.1.

repro_steps: node -e "require('tar').c({file:'/tmp/evil.tar',cwd:'/'},['../../tmp/pwned'])"  # archive with a traversing entry
NEGATIVE CONTROL: repeat with acme-archive@2.4.1 and confirm the entry is rejected and /tmp/pwned is absent
